To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the chemical route to DHAP is limited to the use of toxic reagents or low yields, (ii) the enzymatic route to DHAP requires a multi-enzyme cascade and suffers from complex product mixtues, and that (iii) the combination of chemical and enzymatic routes can lead to improved routes to DHAP.

(1) the DHAP-dependent aldolases can be used to synthesize a variety of vicinal diol products, (2) the DHAP precursor can be synthesized in good yield by a chemical route, and (3) DHAP can be synthesized enzymatically in good yield by using an enzyme cascade.
the chemical and the enzymatic routes to DHAP have their strengths and limitations and that the combination of both approaches may be the key to a practical route to the desired product.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of chemical and enzymatic routes for the synthesis of DHAP.
the development of chemical and enzymatic methods for the synthesis of dihydroxyacetophosphate, the donor substrate for the DHAP-dependent aldolases.
the synthesis of the donor substrate DHAP for the preparative use of DHAP-dependent aldolases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the enzymatic routes to DHAP have been explored to a lesser extent than the chemical ones, and that the enzymatic ones suffer from the need for complex enzyme arrangements.
there is still a need for a better route to DHAP, which is not only applicable on a preparative scale but is also easy to use, safe, and inexpensive.
there is no single route to DHAP that is optimal in every respect, and that the choice of route depends on the particular requirements of a given synthetic project.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the enzymatic routes are more efficient in the production of DHAP, but the chemical routes are more versatile in terms of the range of substrates and the range of downstream reactions that can be coupled to DHAP synthesis.
DHAP is an important synthetic intermediate, and its synthesis has become a well-established field.
we are now able to prepare DHAP in a one-step enzymatic reaction with a yield of 50% and in a two-step enzymatic reaction in 70% yield, both from glucose.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the development of a scalable route to dihydroxy-acetone phosphate (DH-AP) is still an open challenge.
the DHAP-dependent aldolases can be used in preparative synthetic organic chemistry, but that their preparative use requires a reliable source of DHAP.

the DHAP-dependent aldolases are versatile and robust tools in preparative synthetic organic chemistry, and their use in the synthesis of complex molecules will be facilitated by the development of improved routes to DHAP.
